entries.sentence: Parkinson's disease usually develops gradually, and the symptoms are mild at first.
entries.note: NHS symptoms page: usually develops gradually and mild at first.

entries.sentence: The NHS lists three main movement symptoms: tremor, slowed movement and muscle stiffness.
entries.note: NHS symptoms page lists tremor, bradykinesia, rigidity.

entries.sentence: The tremor is shaking that typically starts in a hand or arm and is most noticeable when the limb is at rest.
entries.note: NHS symptoms page tremor description.

entries.sentence: Slowed movement is called bradykinesia, and it can lead to a small-stepped, shuffling walk.
entries.note: NHS symptoms page bradykinesia description.

entries.sentence: Stiffness, also called rigidity, can make movement and facial expression harder and sometimes causes painful cramps.
entries.note: NHS symptoms page rigidity description.

entries.sentence: Symptoms vary a lot from person to person, and it is unlikely that one person would have all or most of them.
entries.note: Search summary of NHS symptoms page: symptoms vary a lot; unlikely to experience all or most.

entries.sentence: The NHS describes the condition as one in which parts of the brain become progressively damaged over many years.
entries.note: Search summary of NHS overview: parts of brain progressively damaged over many years.

entries.sentence: Symptoms tend to worsen over time, and everyday tasks can become harder without help.
entries.note: Search summary statement; page attribution not certain (blended summary).

entries.sentence: Parkinson's also brings symptoms that are not about movement.
entries.note: NHS and NHS inform pages list non-movement symptoms as common.

entries.sentence: NHS inform mentions balance problems, a reduced sense of smell, nerve pain, bladder problems, constipation, sweating, swallowing difficulties, and changes in mood or memory.
entries.note: Search summary listing of NHS inform symptoms.

entries.sentence: Balance problems can make a fall more likely, and a fall can lead to injury.
entries.note: NHS inform: balance problems make falls and injury more likely.

entries.sentence: A loss of the sense of smell sometimes occurs several years before other symptoms develop.
entries.note: Search excerpt: anosmia sometimes occurs several years before other symptoms; page attribution to NHS inform likely but not certain.

entries.sentence: Some of these problems can be treated, and swallowing difficulties, for example, may improve with softer food.
entries.note: Search summary: some can be treated; swallowing may improve with softer food.

entries.sentence: Depression is common in people with Parkinson's, and dementia can develop later in the disease.
entries.note: Search summary: depression common; dementia can develop later; page attribution not certain.

entries.sentence: A review of advanced disease lists motor fluctuations, involuntary movements, falls, hallucinations and sleep disorders among the complications that can occur.
entries.note: Search summary of PMC review 'Treatment of Advanced Parkinson's Disease' listing these complications.

entries.sentence: The NHS says that no test can conclusively show that someone has Parkinson's disease.
entries.note: NHS diagnosis page: no tests can conclusively show Parkinson's.

entries.sentence: A doctor bases the diagnosis on the symptoms, the medical history and a detailed physical examination.
entries.note: NHS diagnosis page quote paraphrased.

entries.sentence: During the examination, the GP may ask the person to do simple movement or walking tasks.
entries.note: NHS diagnosis page summary: GP may ask for simple movement or walking tasks.

entries.sentence: Early on, symptoms are often mild, so a GP may find it hard to be certain.
entries.note: NHS diagnosis page summary.

entries.sentence: If Parkinson's is suspected, the GP usually refers the person to a neurologist or a geriatrician, a specialist in problems affecting older people.
entries.note: NHS diagnosis page summary: referral to neurologist or geriatrician.

entries.sentence: Blood tests and an MRI brain scan may be ordered to rule out other conditions.
entries.note: Search summary; may come from the NHS diagnosis page or trust pages, attribution not certain.

entries.sentence: A DaT scan is a nuclear imaging test that looks at how dopamine transporters work in the brain.
entries.note: Described in hospital patient leaflets returned by the search; NHS diagnosis page attribution not certain.

entries.sentence: It is often used to help tell Parkinson's apart from other causes of tremor or difficulty with movement, and it is only occasionally needed.
entries.note: Hospital leaflets via search summary; attribution to NHS page not certain.

entries.sentence: For the scan, a tracer is injected into a vein and the person lies still, and the results go to the referring doctor, who arranges a follow-up appointment.
entries.note: Hospital DaTSCAN leaflets via search summary; preparation varies by hospital.

entries.sentence: There is currently no cure for Parkinson's disease, but treatments are available to help reduce the main symptoms and maintain quality of life.
entries.note: NHS treatment page summary.

entries.sentence: The NHS lists medicine, supportive therapies such as physiotherapy and occupational therapy, and surgery for some people.
entries.note: NHS treatment page summary.

entries.sentence: Most people with Parkinson's eventually need a medicine called levodopa.
entries.note: NHS treatment page summary.

entries.sentence: MAO-B inhibitors can also improve symptoms, although their effect is small compared with levodopa.
entries.note: NHS treatment page summary.

entries.sentence: People with severe on-off fluctuations or involuntary movements may be considered for medicine delivered continuously through a tube into the tummy.
entries.note: NHS treatment page summary: restricted to people with severe on-off fluctuations or involuntary movements.

entries.sentence: Deep brain stimulation is a type of surgery that does not cure Parkinson's disease but can ease symptoms for some people.
entries.note: NHS treatment page summary.

entries.sentence: It is usually considered when changes to medicines have not controlled the fluctuations in how well they work.
entries.note: NHS treatment page summary: usually considered when fluctuations have not responded to adjustments.

entries.sentence: In the early stages people may need little or no treatment, because symptoms are usually mild at first.
entries.note: Search summary; page attribution not certain.

entries.sentence: Regular exercise can help relieve muscle stiffness, lift mood and reduce stress.
entries.note: NHS 111 Wales page per search summary.

entries.sentence: NHS 111 Wales advises a balanced diet that includes all the food groups.
entries.note: NHS 111 Wales page per search summary.

entries.sentence: Many people with Parkinson's have problems with speech and swallowing.
entries.note: Search summary: swallowing and speech problems; attribution among NHS inform and NHS 111 Wales.

entries.sentence: A speech and language therapist can help with speaking and swallowing exercises.
entries.note: NHS 111 Wales per search summary.

entries.sentence: An occupational therapist can pinpoint everyday tasks that are hard, such as dressing or getting to the shops.
entries.note: NHS 111 Wales per search summary.

entries.sentence: Physiotherapy and occupational therapy are listed by the NHS among the supportive treatments for Parkinson's.
entries.note: NHS treatment page summary.

entries.sentence: Because balance problems can make falls more likely, the NHS inform page flags falls as a risk to be aware of.
entries.note: NHS inform: balance problems make falls more likely.

entries.sentence: Everyday tasks can become harder without help as the condition advances, so practical support from family, carers and health professionals often matters.
entries.note: Search summary says tasks can become harder without help; mention of family and carers is an inference and weakly supported.

entries.sentence: The NHS says that Parkinson's disease does not directly cause people to die, but it can leave them more vulnerable to serious infections.
entries.note: Search summary of NHS page.

entries.sentence: Most people respond to treatment and have only mild to moderate disability.
entries.note: Search summary of NHS outlook wording.

entries.sentence: A minority may not respond as well and can, in time, become more severely disabled.
entries.note: Search summary of NHS page.

entries.sentence: NHS 111 Wales says that most people with Parkinson's now have a normal or near-normal life expectancy.
entries.note: NHS 111 Wales per search summary.

entries.sentence: One study found that respiratory infection was the leading cause of hospital admission among people with the condition.
entries.note: Search summary of PMC study on hospital admissions in Parkinson's disease.

entries.sentence: According to a review of advanced disease, known complications of the condition include falls, motor fluctuations, dementia, hallucinations, sleep disorders and depression.
entries.note: Search summary of PMC review of advanced Parkinson's disease.
